question: Will North Korea launch at least one ballistic missile between September 3 and September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) reports, or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) report citing South Korean, US, or Japanese military/government officials, that North Korea launched at least one ballistic missile at any time between 00:00 September 3, 2026 and 23:59 September 5, 2026, Korea Standard Time (UTC+9). A single launch event involving multiple missiles counts. It resolves NO if no such ballistic-missile launch during that window is reported. A later report confirming a launch that occurred within the window still counts.
reference_class: Rolling 3-day windows in 2026 (Jan 1-Sep 3), asking whether the window contained at least one JCS-reported DPRK ballistic-missile launch event; 12 events over 246 days
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P) [0.07, 0.06, 0.05] -> 0.059; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view (0.07)]
JCS counted 12 ballistic-missile events in 2026 through Aug 20 (~1 per 20.5 days); a random 3-day window contains one ~13-15% of the time, slightly less given events cluster around exercises. As of now (2026-09-04 06:47 KST) all of Sept 3 KST and 7h of Sept 4 have elapsed with no JCS/Japanese/US report of a launch, including the ~5pm KST slot used by the Aug 6, Aug 12 and Aug 20 tests; only ~1.72 of the window's 3 days remain, so 13% x (1.72/3) ~ 7.5%. Last event Aug 20 (14 days quiet), Ulchi Freedom Shield ended Aug 27 and the post-exercise stretch is historically the lull; no anniversary inside the window (Sept 9 founding day falls outside) and Trump-Kim meeting talk is a mild restraint. Small upward offset for a possible Sept 3 launch not yet indexed by my searches - an NK News page rendered Sept 4 still headlined Aug 20. No market matches the contract: Polymarket's 'Number of NK Missile Tests in September 2026' is a whole-month bucketed count (~$22K vol), evidence not anchor; no Kalshi/Manifold/bookmaker equivalent found.
what_would_change_my_mind: Any JCS/NHK/Japan MoD report of a launch on Sept 3 KST that my searches missed - would resolve YES immediately
A newly announced US-ROK drill, B-1B/carrier deployment, or high-profile allied event on Sept 4-5 KST, which historically triggers same-week SRBM salvos
NOTAM/maritime warnings or ROK military statements signaling imminent launch preparations at Wonsan or Sunan
Evidence the Sept 9 founding-anniversary buildup is being marked with weapons tests starting several days early rather than a parade

question: Will SpaceX's Starship Flight 14 (Ship 41) reach orbit between September 3 and September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if the Starship upper stage designated Ship 41, flying on SpaceX's Starship Flight 14 (also referred to as Integrated Flight Test 14), lifts off from Starbase, Texas between 00:00 UTC on September 3, 2026 and 23:59 UTC on September 5, 2026 AND achieves orbit, meaning it completes at least one full revolution around the Earth (a sustained low Earth orbit, as opposed to the suborbital/transatmospheric trajectories of Flights 1-13). Resolution will be based on the entry for Flight 14 (Ship 41) in the "List of Starship launches" Wikipedia page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Starship_launches): the question resolves YES if that entry records the Ship's orbit as "Low Earth orbit" (or an equivalent orbital, non-suborbital classification) for a launch dated within the window, and NO otherwise. If Wikipedia does not clearly reflect the outcome, official SpaceX statements or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
reference_class: Starship integrated flight tests launching within a specific 3-day window beginning ~12 days before the vehicle's then-current publicly stated NET date, with no road closure filed and no launch license announcement at T-2 days
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P) [0.01, 0.01, 0.01] -> 0.010; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view (0.01)]
Two conjunctive requirements: liftoff inside a 3-day window (00:00 Sep 3 – 23:59 Sep 5 UTC, ~50h remaining as of 2026-09-03T21:54Z) AND a completed orbital revolution. The window fails on the first leg. SpaceX's own FCC Special Temporary Authority (signed 2026-08-21) lists start of operations 2026-09-15; the COMPASS manifest slide and launch trackers list Flight 14 as NET 2026-09-15; Wikipedia's Flight 14 infobox reads 'NET early September 2026'. Hardware milestones are done (Booster 21 33-engine static fire Aug 28; Ship 41 six-engine 60s static fire Aug 21) but the operational precursors that reliably appear 2–5 days pre-launch — Cameron County/Starbase SH-4 and Boca Chica Beach closure notices, an FAA license-modification announcement, a scheduled webcast — are all absent for Sep 3–5. Starship launch dates have never moved earlier than a publicly stated NET; slips are one-directional. Human markets: searched Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold — no contract matching this question's terms found; Polymarket's space section has only a loosely related 'how many Starship launches reach space in 2026' market (~$10.4M section-wide volume, not this event, different threshold and no date window), so it is not a usable anchor. Residual 1% covers an undetected surprise-fast turnaround plus the ~70% conditional odds that a first-ever orbital insertion actually closes an orbit.
what_would_change_my_mind: A Cameron County / City of Starbase road closure or beach closure notice naming September 3, 4, or 5, 2026
SpaceX announcing a webcast or an FAA launch-license modification for Flight 14 dated within the window
A revised FCC/marine navigation warning or updated COMPASS manifest moving Flight 14 earlier than September 15

question: Will Sony announce a new PlayStation State of Play showcase between September 3 and September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, at any time from 00:00 UTC on September 3, 2026 through 23:59 UTC on September 5, 2026, Sony Interactive Entertainment officially announces a new "State of Play" broadcast (a livestreamed PlayStation showcase presenting game news and trailers), as posted on the official PlayStation.Blog (https://blog.playstation.com/) or reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). The announcement counts regardless of when the broadcast itself is scheduled to air. Otherwise it resolves NO.
reference_class: 2.1-day calendar windows containing a first-time Sony announcement of a new State of Play broadcast, 2023-2026 (~5-7 distinct SoP/SoP-Japan/dedicated-SoP announcements per year), further conditioned on the window opening the same day a State of Play aired
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P) [0.03, 0.09, 0.06] -> 0.055; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view (0.03)]
The Sept 3 State of Play and State of Play Japan were announced Aug 31 on PlayStation.Blog, i.e. before the window opens, and the fine print explicitly excludes re-promotion of a pre-window announcement. Both aired Sept 3 (6am PT); as of 2026-09-03T21:58Z the Blog front page carries only recap/game posts and no new broadcast announcement. That leaves ~50h (Fri Sept 4, Sat Sept 5) for a brand-new State of Play announcement the day after Sony ran a two-hour double showcase — a pattern with no historical precedent; Sony's inter-SoP gap is typically 2-4 months and announcements land Mon-Wed, so Saturday is near-dead. Residual probability covers a surprise dedicated single-game SoP (e.g. a Marvel's Wolverine deep dive ahead of its launch) or a TGS-tied announcement pulled forward, plus resolver ambiguity. No human prediction market prices this contract.
what_would_change_my_mind: A PlayStation.Blog post or official PlayStation social post dated Sept 4-5 naming a new 'State of Play' (e.g. a dedicated Marvel's Wolverine or TGS-tied broadcast)
Credible reporting that Sony teased a further State of Play at the end of the Sept 3 or Sept 3 Japan broadcast
Evidence Sony has previously announced a follow-up State of Play within 72 hours of one airing

question: Will the M/V LUTUF and its crew be freed from pirate control before September 5, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if the M/V LUTUF — the Cameroon-flagged cargo vessel hijacked on 17 August 2026 off Puntland, Somalia — and its crew are confirmed to have been freed from the control of the hijackers before 23:59 UTC on September 4, 2026. "Freed" means the crew (or the surviving/remaining crew) is confirmed to be no longer under the physical control of the hijackers, whether by negotiated release, naval/military rescue, escape, or the hijackers abandoning the vessel and crew. It resolves NO if, as of 23:59 UTC on September 4, 2026, no such confirmation has occurred and the vessel and/or crew remain under hijacker control (this is the default). Resolution is based on official statements from EU NAVFOR Operation ATALANTA (https://eunavfor.eu/news) or reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
reference_class: Somali pirate hijackings of merchant vessels 2024-2026, resolved (crew out of hijacker control) within ~18 days of seizure
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P) [0.97, 0.97, 0.97] -> 0.970; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view (0.97)]
Reference class: Somali hijackings 2024-26 resolved within ~18 days of seizure — roughly 1 in 4, so an unconditional prior near 0.25. But this is an already-resolved check, and it fires: multiple independent credible outlets (AP via WTOP 30 Aug, Somali Guardian 29 Aug, Hiiraan, DefenceWeb, Rio Times) report the LUTUF and its crew freed on 29 August 2026, five days before the 4 Sept cutoff. Somalia's defence ministry credits a joint Turkish-Somali operation (14 pirates killed, four skiffs destroyed); Puntland says a ~$2.5m ransom was paid and the pirates left voluntarily — the accounts conflict on mechanism, agree that the pirates no longer control the ship, and either mechanism satisfies the criterion. A local elder quoted by AP confirmed vessel and crew. Deductions: EU NAVFOR ATALANTA (the named precedence source) has published no LUTUF liberation notice on its visible newsroom, and no government has formally confirmed crew welfare, leaving a narrow path for a strict resolver to call confirmation insufficient; no evidence of re-capture. 0.97.
what_would_change_my_mind: An EU NAVFOR ATALANTA or UKMTO statement dated after 29 Aug still listing LUTUF among vessels under pirate control
Reporting that the 29 Aug release was retracted, or that the vessel/crew were re-taken before 4 Sept 23:59 UTC
Credible reporting that only the vessel was released while some crew were taken ashore as hostages

question: Will Ethereum's closing price exceed $2,500 on September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if the daily closing price of Ethereum (ETH) in US dollars for September 4, 2026 (UTC) is greater than $2,500.00, as reported on CoinGecko's Ethereum price history page: https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum/historical_data (the "Close" value for the row dated 2026-09-04). Otherwise it resolves NO. For example, a close of $2,501.34 resolves YES; a close of $2,499.99 or $2,500.00 resolves NO.
reference_class: ETH 1-day-ahead close vs a strike ~0.4% below spot, using the observed distribution of ETH/USD daily log returns over the trailing 13 sessions (Aug 21 - Sep 2, 2026; SD 2.41%)
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P) [0.55, 0.52, 0.52] -> 0.530; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view (0.55)]
Resolution is CoinGecko's Close for the 2026-09-04 UTC row, verified to equal the 2026-09-05T00:00Z print (the Sep-2 row's Close, $2,390.78, matches the Sep-3 00:00Z snapshot). Spot at 2026-09-03T22:08Z is $2,509.55 on CoinGecko ($2,506.36 Binance), i.e. 0.38% above the $2,500 strike with ~25.9h left, after a short-squeeze spike from $2,396 to $2,517 between 15:00-19:00Z that has since consolidated. Base rate: of the trailing 13 ETH daily log returns (SD 2.41%), 7 exceeded -0.38%, giving 54%; the lognormal equivalent over 1.078 days gives 55.6%. Polymarket's Sep-4 bracket book, normalized for a 3.9% overround, implies ~55% above $2,500 -- but it settles on Binance ETHUSDT at 16:00Z, 8h earlier, on thin liquidity ($814 liquidity on the pivotal bracket), so it corroborates rather than anchors. Main counterargument: post-squeeze giveback plus the August NFP print at 12:30Z Sep 4 (consensus +56k after -23k) sits inside the window, and a 0.4% cushion is well under one hourly candle's range -- but that risk is two-sided and already in the vol estimate.
what_would_change_my_mind: ETH breaking decisively out of the $2,490-2,530 chop before 00:00Z Sep 4 — a sustained hold above ~$2,560 or a drop under ~$2,450 would move this 15+ points either way
A large NFP surprise on Sep 4 at 12:30Z (consensus +56k) driving a risk-on or risk-off move greater than ~1.5% in ETH
Deeper Polymarket/Kalshi liquidity on a same-day $2,500 threshold contract pricing materially away from ~55%
Escalation of the US-Iran strikes or oil above ~$100/bbl reviving the risk-off bid that produced the $2,391 two-week low earlier on Sep 3
A reversal in ETH spot-ETF flows (Sep 2 saw a $48m outflow ending a 12-day inflow streak)

question: Will U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs record a single-day net inflow exceeding $500 million on any trading day between August 31 and September 7, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, on any U.S. equity trading day from August 31, 2026 through September 4, 2026 (inclusive), the aggregate net flow across all U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs is greater than +$500 million (i.e. a value above 500.0 in the "Total" row, expressed in US$m), as reported in the Bitcoin ETF Flow table at https://farside.co.uk/btc/ . For example, a "Total" of 606.3 for a given date resolves YES; a "Total" of 307.5 does not. Otherwise it resolves NO. (September 7, 2026 is Labor Day, when U.S. equity markets and these ETFs do not trade, so no flows occur on that date.)
reference_class: US spot Bitcoin ETF trading days in 2026 with aggregate single-day net flow above +$500m (Farside Total row)
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P) [0.17, 0.05, 0.15] -> 0.110; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view (0.17)]
Window is Aug 31-Sep 4 (5 sessions; Sep 7 is Labor Day). Three are already reported and all far below: Aug 31 +216.7, Sep 1 -236.5 (largest outflow since Jul 31), Sep 2 +101.2. Only Sep 3 (traded, publishing tonight) and Sep 4 remain. Reference class: 2026 trading days with aggregate net flow >+$500m ~3%/day (Jan cluster incl. a $753m session, Feb, then Aug 19 +517.2 and Aug 20 +606.3 - explicitly the largest in ~3.5 months, so none between early May and mid-Aug). Two remaining days unconditionally ~6%. Upward conditioning: BTC +5.5% on Sep 3 to ~$81.5k on Fed rate-pause signals, Saylor resumed buying $370m, and August was the best flow month of 2026 (+$3.52bn), so a spike day is live. Downward: the threshold needs ~5x the current daily run-rate and IBIT near $300-500m alone (IBIT was only +$115m Sep 2, -$201m Sep 1); GBTC is still bleeding; flows lag price and much of Sep 3's move came late-session; 2026 remains net-outflow YTD (-$1.77bn). Sep 4's figure also publishes right at the resolution timestamp, a small extra NO tilt. P(Sep 3)~0.12, P(Sep 4|not Sep 3)~0.07 -> ~0.17. No matching human market: Polymarket's daily ETF-flow contracts use the same Farside Total row but resolve on sign only (>0 / <0), not a $500m threshold, and the Sep 3 event shows 50/50 on $0 volume - a near-miss contract, not an anchor.
what_would_change_my_mind: Farside posts a Sept 3 Total above ~$400m, or IBIT alone above ~$300m, indicating a flow regime shift into Sept 4
BTC extends the rally hard on Sept 4 (e.g. through $85k) with reports of large creations
A Sept 3 Total that is flat or negative despite the 5.5% price rally, which would confirm flows are decoupled and push this below 8%
